new_scholarship.deadline: The deadline for application-based scholarships is January 10. For undergraduate students starting at the U of A in September 2027, the scholarship application will open Oct. 1, 2026 and close Jan. 10, 2027.
new_scholarship.application_period: Entrance scholarship applications through the U of A Awards Hub run from Oct. 1 to Jan. 10. For students starting in September 2027 the window opens October 1, 2026 and closes January 10, 2027. Offers are made starting in early winter.
new_scholarship.application_method: Separate application, not automatic on admission. The University of Alberta states: 'You must apply to an undergraduate degree program before you can apply for any entrance scholarships.' Applicants then submit one single scholarship application through the U of A Awards Hub (https://alberta.academicworks.ca/), which assesses them for all application-based awards including this one. Admission-based awards by contrast require no scholarship application and are assessed from the admission average at the time of the admission offer; this award is listed among the application-based awards.
new_scholarship.description: The President's International Distinction Scholarship is the University of Alberta's most prestigious and competitive scholarship for international students. Each year 25 students with a superior admission average and demonstrated leadership qualities entering their first year of an undergraduate degree on a student visa permit receive up to CAN $120,000, payable over four years. It is an application-based award: applicants must first apply to an undergraduate degree program, then submit the University's single scholarship application, which for September 2027 entry closes January 10, 2027. The University of Alberta states that it does not offer full scholarships for either domestic or international students, so this award does not cover the whole cost of an international degree.
new_scholarship.best_fit: High-achieving applicants from outside Canada who will enter the first year of a full-time undergraduate degree at the University of Alberta on a student visa permit, have a superior admission average, and can evidence leadership in school, community organisations, extracurricular activities or the workplace. Published winners have entered BEng, BSc, BAEcon, BCom, BA/BSc and BSc (Hons) programmes across Engineering, Science, Arts and Business.
new_scholarship.eligibility_summary: Applicants must be entering directly from high school, must be entering the first year of full-time studies in an undergraduate degree program at the University of Alberta in September of the upcoming year, must be studying on a student visa permit, must meet or exceed the required admission average (the award page describes this as a 'superior admission average') and must demonstrate leadership qualities. An admission application must be submitted before any entrance scholarship application can be made. Entrance award offers are conditional on the accuracy of self-recorded grades. No nationality restriction is published; published winners came from India, Costa Rica, China, Colombia, Mexico and Nigeria.

new_scholarship.selection_notes: The University of Alberta uses a single application form to assess applicants for all application-based awards, based on academics, leadership, inclusion and financial need. For this award the published criteria are a superior admission average plus demonstrated leadership qualities. 25 awards are made each year. The University states that scholarship and award competitions are competitive and that there is no guarantee that meeting eligibility will result in an offer, and that entrance award offers are conditional on the accuracy of self-recorded grades, with the offer revocable where those grades differ from the final official transcript. No published selection weighting percentages.
new_scholarship.notes: Award selection: the University of Alberta publishes several bachelor's-level international undergraduate awards. This is the one recorded because it is the best documented of them, publishing an exact value (up to CAN $120,000), a payment duration (over 4 years), a published award count (25 each year), a single published deadline (January 10) and a clear eligibility basis. No second record was produced for any other ualberta.ca international award, so there is no duplicate-award conflict. Confirmed absent from backend/config/programme_details.json by grep (no record mentions Alberta or ualberta); the only 'Alberta' hits in backend/config/new_scholarships.json are unrelated graduate awards (Alberta Innovates Graduate Student Scholarships, MOPGA). No bond or service obligation is published for this award. The award is a cash scholarship, not a named tuition waiver; no separate living-cost component is published.

programme_detail_official.description: The President's International Distinction Scholarship is the University of Alberta's most prestigious and competitive scholarship for international students. Each year 25 students with a superior admission average and demonstrated leadership qualities entering their first year of an undergraduate degree on a student visa permit receive up to CAN $120,000, payable over four years. It is an application-based award: applicants must first apply to an undergraduate degree program, then submit the University's single scholarship application by January 10, and offers are made starting in early winter. The University of Alberta states that it does not offer full scholarships for either domestic or international students, so the award funds part rather than all of the cost of an international degree.
programme_detail_official.coverage: Cash scholarship of up to CAN $120,000 payable over four years, to 25 recipients per year. Not a full-cost award. The University of Alberta's International Tuition + Fees page identifies the four cost components of an international degree - instructional tuition fees, non-instructional fees, books and supplies, and living arrangement - none of which is separately covered by this award.

application_readiness_checklist: Submit your University of Alberta undergraduate degree program application first; you cannot apply for any entrance scholarship until you have applied, and the CCID and password needed to apply for scholarships can take two to three business days to generate
Submit the single U of A scholarship application through the Awards Hub between Oct. 1 and Jan. 10; for September 2027 entry the deadline is January 10, 2027
Aim for a superior admission average, since this is the University's most competitive international award with only 25 places each year
Document leadership in school, community organizations, extracurricular activities or the workplace, because the award requires demonstrated leadership qualities
Ensure you will be studying on a student visa permit, as the award is restricted to student visa permit holders
Record your self-recorded grades carefully; the University of Alberta states offers are conditional on their accuracy and can be revoked on discrepancy
Plan to accept the admission offer and pay the tuition deposit by the published award-acceptance deadline, which is what keeps the entrance scholarship
If you need accessibility support to complete the application, request applicant accommodations or contact sse@ualberta.ca before the deadline
common_rejection_risks: Applying for the scholarship before submitting an admission application to an undergraduate degree program
Missing the January 10 scholarship application deadline, or applying in the wrong window; transfer and continuing students apply Feb. 1 to Mar. 31, which is not this award
An admission average that is not superior; with 25 awards against all entering international students, competition is severe
Inability to evidence leadership qualities through the single application form
Self-recorded grades that differ from the final official transcript, which the University of Alberta states can cause the award offer to be revoked
Expecting the award to cover the whole cost of an international degree; the University of Alberta states it does not offer full scholarships for domestic or international students
estimated_uncovered_costs: The balance of instructional tuition fees for the four years of the degree; the award is a capped cash scholarship, and the University of Alberta states it does not offer full scholarships
Non-instructional fees, which the University's International Tuition + Fees page lists as one of the four main cost factors
Books and supplies, listed as a separate main cost factor by the University
Living arrangement costs, whether in residence or off campus, listed as a separate main cost factor by the University
Health and dental coverage; the University states international students are enrolled by default for health and dental coverage through Alumo (formerly Studentcare)

Up-front cash-flow costs: a CAD $150 application fee for new students, and a CAD $5,000 tuition deposit required to accept the admission offer and receive the Provincial Attestation Letter (CAD $1,000 for students already studying in Canada)
Study permit fees, first-entry costs, travel to Canada and any other costs not named in the published provision
document_audit: Confirm the undergraduate admission application has already been submitted and the CCID has been issued before starting the scholarship application
Keep an accurate record of the self-recorded grades used for admission, because the offer is conditional on them

Assemble leadership evidence across school, community, extracurricular and workplace contexts before writing the single application form, since the same form is reused for all application-based awards
Ensure the application is submitted through the Awards Hub and not by email; the University publishes the Awards Hub as the route

logo_override.validation_detail: Probed live on 2026-10-03: HTTP 200, Content-Type image/jpeg, 41,385 bytes, leading bytes ffd8ffe1 (JPEG SOI marker followed by an EXIF APP1 segment), so the response is genuine JPEG image data and not an HTML error page or WAF interstitial. The asset is published as the og:image and twitter:image:src of the official ualberta.ca homepage and is the institution's own wordmark, so it is the awarding body's mark and not the logo of a different body. As a JPEG it has no alpha channel, so it cannot be a white-on-transparent wordmark.

research_notes.logo: Logo hunt order followed. (1) Probed https://www.ualberta.ca/en/index.html and extracted every logo-referencing src/href/content attribute from the page markup; the only institution-mark asset found was https://www.ualberta.ca/en/media-library/ualberta/homepage/university-of-alberta-logo.jpg. (2) Confirmed independently that the same URL is declared as og:image and twitter:image:src on the official homepage, which establishes it as the University's own chosen mark. (3) Probed the bytes live: HTTP 200, Content-Type image/jpeg, 41,385 bytes, JPEG SOI magic ffd8ffe1 - image data, not HTML, so rule 7 is satisfied. (4) Rule 6 is satisfied structurally: the asset is a JPEG with no alpha channel, so a white-on-transparent wordmark is impossible; it is the green UAlberta wordmark on a light background. Served from www.ualberta.ca, the awarding body's own domain, so official_host is true and host_evidence is same_registrable_domain. Also probed https://www.ualberta.ca/apple-touch-icon.png (HTTP 200, image/png, 10,786 bytes, PNG magic 89504e47) and https://www.ualberta.ca/favicon.ico (HTTP 200, image/vnd.microsoft.icon, 15,086 bytes, ICO magic 00000100) as fallbacks, but the JPEG wordmark was preferred over a square app icon. Not used at all: any aggregator, CDN, Wikimedia or social-host asset. logo_host_taken is false for slot b100, so this is a new key for host ualberta.ca and not a duplicate.

research_notes.degree_level_confirmed: The International Entrance Scholarships page states the award is for students 'entering their first year of an undergraduate degree on a student visa permit'. This is independently corroborated by the Entrance Scholarships page, whose Eligibility Requirements state applicants must be 'entering the first year of full-time studies in an undergraduate degree program at the U of A in September of the upcoming year', and by the President's International Distinction Scholarship Winners page, where published recipients are listed by their bachelor's programmes (BEng, BSc, BAEcon, BCom, BA/BSc, BSc (Hons)) across the Faculties of Engineering, Science, Arts and Business.
research_notes.award_selection_rationale: Slot b100 was 'University of Alberta International Scholarships', which names a family of awards rather than a single award. University of Alberta publishes several bachelor's-level international undergraduate awards on one host: the President's International Distinction Scholarship (up to CAN $120,000 over 4 years, 25 per year), the Chan Pang Kuen Memorial International Distinction Scholarship (up to CAN $120,000 over 4 years), the May Quon Undergraduate Scholarship (up to CAN $100,000 over 4 years), the Cora Martinson International Scholarship (up to CAN $56,000 over 4 years), the International Leader Scholarship (up to CAN $15,000), the University of Alberta Global Citizen Scholarship for Aga Khan Academy IB students (full tuition and non-instructional fees for four years plus up to $28,000 per year), and the admission-based International Admission and Regional Excellence Scholarships. The President's International Distinction Scholarship was chosen because it is the single best documented of them: it is the only one whose page publishes an exact value, a payment duration, an award count, a deadline and a stated eligibility basis together, and it is described by the University as its most prestigious and competitive international scholarship. The others are recorded as a cross-check against the richer domestic awards in the Entrance Scholarships page, not as separate records, so there is no duplicate-award conflict on this host.
